title: The distance to a tidal source
hook: Change distance to the source and predict leading tidal acceleration difference.
misconception: leading tidal acceleration difference doubles when distance to the source doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply tidal acceleration difference ≈ 2GMℓ/r³ to compare leading tidal acceleration difference when distance to the source changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a small fixed radial separation much shorter than the distance from a fixed point-mass source, tidal acceleration difference ≈ 2GMℓ/r³. When distance to the source doubles, leading tidal acceleration difference becomes ⅛ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model tidal acceleration difference ≈ 2GMℓ/r³; scaling exponent -3. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a small fixed radial separation much shorter than the distance from a fixed point-mass source, with a nonzero initial result. If distance to the source triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on leading tidal acceleration difference?
recall.why: Apply tidal acceleration difference ≈ 2GMℓ/r³ under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/27.
